steps.purpose: Plan the release without performing it: ordered steps with exact commands and authority, rollback, the release test plan, post-release consumer_checks and consumer_entry.
steps.directive_evidence: Stating the gates helped but did not stop the source reading: 318 s, 41 calls, 21 ShipLoop-source reads and 0 refusals, against chess's 748 s, 64 calls and 34 reads. The remaining reads targeted what Checked-by names but does not define: 'Checking allowed_consumers and whether release-check executes consumer_checks or the host does'; 'Checking the navigator to see if the release-plan rejects unnamed consumer commands'; the 'shaped like test_commands' row (it read shiploop_test_loop.normalise_commands); and placeholders. It spent about 1.5k characters of THINK on the present/absent rule: 'The grant forbids deleting metadata, so a pre-release absent observation cannot be produced.'
steps.response: The plan served its purpose. It gives validate, deploy, assign, confirm and source return, each with an owner and the grant; the rollback copied from the packet's recipes; a consumer_entry (App Launcher, SLBattle, SLBattle Board, 4 source files); one consumer check; and A1 for release-verify. Three latent defects shipped: (1) the dry run 'sf project deploy validate --target-org de' lacks --source-dir and exited 2 at release-check; (2) git status showed '?? .sf/' and the plan did nothing about it, so plan-return later committed it and forced a working-tree-return; (3) the confirm check observes the classes and the permission set only, not the app or tab.
gaps: The present/absent confirm rule assumes the target is untouched before release. Here every test command deploys to org de, so 'absent' cannot be observed and both release-plan and release-check had to work around it. Fix: 'If earlier stages already placed the candidate on the target, cite the last recorded absent observation and expect present at release-check.' Generated at shiploop_prompts.py:1716 (release-plan item 5), shiploop_prompts.py:1744 (release-check item 4) and shiploop_stage_spec.py:574 (release-check done-when).

'consumer_checks, shaped like test_commands' points to a schema the packet does not contain. Fix: print the row inline as {command, suite: check|focused|regression, ids?, min_tests?}. Generated at shiploop_prompts.py:1718.

Nothing tells release-plan that plan-return commits every untracked path, including tool state such as .sf/. Fix: release-plan item 8 should add: 'list untracked tool-state directories; add them to .gitignore or plan them as --exclude before release-check runs plan-return'. Better, fix commit_leftovers itself (see 49). Generated at shiploop_workspace.py:1294.

The consumer check does not have to observe the consumer entry. Fix: 'at least one consumer check observes what consumer_entry names on the target (here CustomTab SLBattle_Board and CustomApplication SLBattle)'. Generated at shiploop_prompts.py:1718-1725.

The template rule says to replace every <...> placeholder, but the packet's own rollback recipe contains '<kept paths>'. The model planned around a refusal that does not exist, because _placeholders only walks the hand-off fields. Fix: print the recipe with the return plan's keep rows filled in, or say the recipe text is exempt.

steps.purpose: Observe the released result where consumers use it, run the consumer checks, record consumer cases this host cannot observe as open items, and write the run's lessons.
steps.directive_evidence: 236 s, 50 calls. The context was reset mid-stage (SAY 'The run is still on release-verify. I'll reload the current packet'). It made 19 ShipLoop-source reads and 10 guide reads, mostly to choose the open item's consumer: THINK 'Setting the consumer to operations settles A1 via its done result ... could remove the open item before handoff ... The best consumer is handoff.' It followed item 6 and did not block: 'The run is unattended, so blocking the release was avoided.' The packet quoted A1 five times (from verify, carry-forward, system-test-author, system-test and release-plan) plus A9.
steps.response: It met the unattended contract. The confirm passed in the clean consumer copy. Source sync, identity, receipt and behaviour were kept as four separate facts. SYS-BOARD (S4, S15, S20, S21) is not-run, recorded as A1 with consumer handoff. The lessons are concrete: validate needs --source-dir, a duplicate assign exits 1, and .sf forced the working-tree-return. Chess's release-verify, by contrast, blocked twice (369 s + 3,402 s) and never finished. Was the person's ask answerable? Partly. A Salesforce user can follow App Launcher, SLBattle, SLBattle Board and the boardClick steps in docs/shiploop/architecture.md, which was returned to the checkout. But the ask gives no URL path, lists 'six observations' that do not match the 5-step boardClick procedure (which also checks the New game reset, the repeat-click error and that unfired cells stay blank), forbids the person the easiest route ('Do not run sf org open' is the agent's credential rule), names a conditional owner, and gives no yes/no form or reply channel. Its consumer is handoff, which settles it simply by finishing.
gaps: Item 6 does not name the consumer for an open item only a person can act on, so the model read stage_spec and assumptions source to pick handoff over operations. Fix: 'record it with consumer handoff'. Generated at shiploop_prompts.py:1794-1802.

The fill-in form ('step 1 reaches the consumer entry (menu entry or URL path) ...; report is a fill-in list, one yes/no line per case') applies only to a blocked/awaiting ask. A person-owned open item gets free text with no reply route. Fix: require the same entry line and yes/no lines in every person-owned open item's check, carry them into report.html as a checklist, and drop agent-only prohibitions from asks addressed to a person. Generated at shiploop_prompts.py:1794-1802; open-row fields in shiploop_assumptions.py _FIELDS.

Every stage re-listed the same open item, so release-verify's packet quotes A1 five times. Fix: dedupe by id and text in the packet, and tell stages 'an open item already recorded for a later consumer stays open; do not re-list it'. Generated at shiploop_navigator.py:5640-5652 (_source_lines for assumptions) and in the open-item duties (shiploop_prompts.py:1608, 1641, 1724).

The opposite case appears at 43 and 47: 'open items: none open' was printed while A1 and A2 were open for later stages. The list is filtered to this stage's consumer, but the label does not say so. Fix: 'open items due here: none (N open for later stages)'. Generated at shiploop_navigator.py:5644.

The model then ended its turn: Grok logged shell.handle_prompt.done ok:true at 06:47:23Z, and the keepalive Stop hook logged 'allow: run is done'. run_level.step_by_step: This group has no implement or step stages (outer stages 43-53). The outer stages ran strictly in graph order, one stage per packet, each submitted with check-only and then complete. There were zero refusals in 11 steps and no replan, repeat or blocked outcome. The release half took 23 min of wall time (2 h 18 min to 2 h 41 min on the pace line, two Improve reviews included). The nine non-Improve stages used 1,324 model seconds; chess's same stages used 5,541 s and stopped blocked at release-verify.
run_level.improve: There were two Improve reviews; each was trivial, took one pass and made no edits. 44 (40 s, 9 calls) was correct because nothing was wrong. 48 (107 s, 14 calls) was a partial rubber stamp: it probed the confirm query (exit 0) but skipped the planned validate as 'deployment-like'. Release-check caught that 'sf project deploy validate' was missing --source-dir (exit 2) one stage later. 48 also waved off the consumer check's failure to observe the app or tab, a limit the run's lessons still carry. Neither review found a real problem; release-check's own dry run was the effective check in this half.
run_level.directive: Scale 1-5: 5 = executed from the packet alone; 3 = right method but had to read ShipLoop source for a shape or rule; 1 = guessed or misled. Scores: 43:3, 44:4, 45:5, 46:2, 47:3, 48:3, 49:4, 50:5, 51:2, 52:5, 53:4. There were 66 ShipLoop-source reads (43:7, 46:19, 47:21, 51:19), all in the four stages that write an open-item or hand-off list whose row shape and allowed consumers the packet does not print. Two context resets (46, 51) forced re-learning. Stages whose packet carried the whole contract (system-test, release, operations) took 42-73 s with no source reads. Release-plan: stating the gates worked partly. It took 318 s (5.3 min per index.json; the brief's 3 min does not match), 41 calls, 21 source reads and 0 refusals, against chess's 748 s, 64 calls and 34 reads. The reads that remain target what Checked-by names but does not define: allowed consumers, the open-row shape, 'shaped like test_commands', and whether ## Commands must name the confirm command.
run_level.after_done: Last THINK: 'The ShipLoop run is complete. I will present the final narrative and summarize the outcome, including the commit request.' The final SAY ended with a request that the absent user commit the working-tree return. The turn ended at 06:47:23Z and keepalive allowed the stop ('run is done'). The Grok process then idled 30 min 23 s until it was killed (rc 143). The idle was the host not exiting, not the model.

best: system-test: complete reused the check-only rerun ('That complete takes this test run ... instead of running the commands again'), so the stage took 41.7 s and 4 calls with no reasoning detours.
release-verify item 6 plus the Unattended rule: the unobservable board was recorded as an open item instead of a block. The stage finished in 236 s; chess blocked twice (3,771 s) and never finished.
The packet prints the return route and copy-ready rollback recipes with SHAs. Release-plan copied them without searching, release returned in one command, and handoff verified the receipt.
Checked-by gate lists plus complete --check-only: zero refusals across all 11 steps.
release-check items 3-4 ('run the dry-run form ... once'; 'fixed now ... and rerun') caught and fixed the plan's broken validate command before the real deploy.
worst: OUTER open-item stages get "assumptions": [] with no row shape and no list of allowed consumers (shiploop_navigator.py:4135-4136), and the gate is worded as a double negative (shiploop_navigator.py:5934). Together they cost 66 ShipLoop-source reads in 43, 46, 47 and 51, and one misread ('The packet forbids open items whose consumer is a later outer stage').

commit_leftovers (shiploop_workspace.py:1294) committed untracked .sf/ tracking files at release-check, and review-return then excluded them. The result was a working-tree-return with no commit on main: the E2E 'committed' check failed (HEAD 45e3cc53, 0 files, 18 uncommitted) and the done packet asked an absent user to commit.

The Improve handoff's 'does not execute or replay a release effect (a deployment ...)' (shiploop_prompts.py:2765) does not exempt dry runs, so the release-plan review skipped validate and missed its exit 2.

The person-only board ask is not ready for a reply. It gives no URL path, lists 'six observations' against a 5-step boardClick procedure, forbids the person 'sf org open' (an agent-only rule), and has no yes/no form and no consumer to receive an answer (handoff settles it by finishing).

The same open item A1 was re-listed by five stages and quoted five times at release-verify. Meanwhile 43 and 47 printed 'open items: none open' while A1 and A2 were open for later stages (shiploop_navigator.py:5640-5652).
